# Toasts, drawers and overlays (house standards, version 4)

<!-- generated by tools/build_data.py from synthesis/; edit the source, not this file -->

How toasts (Sonner), drawers and sheets (Vaul and native sheets), tooltips, menus and modals are built, placed, stacked, timed and dismissed.

Rules from non-negotiable sources. **must**: never break it without the person's explicit override. **should**: the default; say so when you depart from it. How to change one: `../standards.md`.

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-02: Mount one Toaster at the root
**must** · react. Mount exactly one <Toaster /> once, as close to the app root as possible (in Next.js, layout.tsx), and never render it per page, conditionally, or in both a layout and a page.
- Values: mount: <Toaster />; next.js: layout.tsx
- Why: A second mounted Toaster duplicates every toast, and an unmounted one means toasts never appear.
- Sources: S-L19-022, S-L19-022, S-L19-087, S-L19-088

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-03: Keep the Toaster outside stacking contexts
**should** · web, react. Mount the Toaster at the document root, outside any dialog or portal container and outside any ancestor with transform, filter or overflow.
- Values: avoid-ancestors: transform, filter, overflow
- Why: Such an ancestor creates a stacking context, or the overlay out-z-indexes the toaster, so toasts sit behind a modal or get clipped.
- Sources: S-L19-022

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-04: Call toast() only from client code
**must** · react. Call toast() only from client code (event handlers, effects, callbacks); in a server action, return the result and call toast() in the client code that receives it.
- Why: toast() is a plain function that does nothing on the server.
- Sources: S-L19-022, S-L19-087

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-05: Fire toasts from handlers or stable ids
**should** · react. Fire toasts from event handlers; when a toast must fire from an effect, pass a stable id so a repeated call updates the toast instead of duplicating it.
- Values: effect-fix: stable id
- Why: React StrictMode's dev double-invoke runs effects twice; a stable id makes the second call update rather than duplicate.
- Sources: S-L19-022

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-07: Web toast enter: 400ms ease from below
**should** · web, css, react. On the web, enter a toast from opacity: 0 and transform: translateY(100%) to its settled position with transition: opacity 400ms ease, transform 400ms ease, using @starting-style (or a mounted flag set in useEffect where @starting-style is unavailable).
- Values: from: opacity: 0; transform: translateY(100%); transition: opacity 400ms ease, transform 400ms ease; entry: @starting-style; fallback: useEffect(() => { setMounted(true); }, []); <div data-mounted={mounted}>
- Why: A toast that suddenly appears feels off; Sonner uses ease rather than ease-out and runs slightly slower than typical UI because its motion is tuned to the component's personality.
- Sources: S-L19-006, S-L19-012, S-L19-017, S-L19-023, S-L19-024

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-08: React Native toasts: 300ms in, 250ms out
**must** · react-native, ios, android. In React Native, enter toasts with FadeInDown.duration(300).easing(EASE_OUT), exit with FadeOutDown.duration(250).easing(EASE_OUT), keep them within the 300ms cap, and define both builders at module scope.
- Values: enter: FadeInDown.duration(300).easing(EASE_OUT); exit: FadeOutDown.duration(250).easing(EASE_OUT); cap: 300ms; exit-vs-enter: ~20% faster; EASE_OUT: Easing.bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)
- Why: A toast is uninvited, so it should be quicker and quieter than motion the user asked for; the user has finished reading, so the exit runs about 20% faster than the entry.
- Sources: S-L19-015, S-L19-015

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-10: Stack toasts with lift and depth
**should** · web, css. In the collapsed stack, position toasts absolutely, lift each toast behind the front one by the gap times its index, and scale it down by 0.05 per index; apply this only to non-front toasts while the stack is collapsed.
- Values: scale: scale(calc((-1 * var(--toasts-before) * 0.05) + 1)); lift: translateY(calc(var(--lift-amount) * var(--toasts-before))); examples: Y(0) scale(1); Y(-14px) scale(0.95); Y(-28px) scale(0.9); selector: [data-sonner-toast][data-expanded="false"][data-front="false"]
- Why: Absolute positioning simplifies the stacking, and scaling the toasts behind down creates a sense of depth.
- Sources: S-L19-006

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-11: Stacked toasts share the front height
**should**. While toasts are stacked, give every toast the height of the toast in front.
- Why: Toasts with different heights otherwise do not stick out evenly behind the front toast.
- Sources: S-L19-006

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-12: Expand the toast stack on hover
**should** · web, react. Keep the toast stack collapsed and expand it while the pointer hovers the toast area (expand: false by default); when expanded, offset each toast by its index times the gap plus the heights of the toasts before it, with a gap of 14.
- Values: expand: false (default); offset: heightIndex * GAP + toastsHeightBefore; gap: 14
- Why: Stacked mode hides older toasts and hovering reveals them; toasts can differ in height, so each expanded offset adds the real heights above it.
- Sources: S-L19-006, S-L19-021, S-L19-021, S-L19-092

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-13: Fill gaps between toasts for hover
**must** · web, css. Fill the gaps between expanded toasts with an :after pseudo-element so the hover state holds while the pointer crosses a gap.
- Values: css: :after
- Why: The gaps belong to no toast, so hovering them would make the toasts lose their hover state (and collapse).
- Sources: S-L19-006, S-L19-023

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-14: Show at most three toasts
**should** · web, react. Show at most 3 toasts at once by default (visibleToasts: 3).
- Values: visibleToasts: 3
- Why: 3 is Sonner's documented default number of visible toasts.
- Sources: S-L19-021, S-L19-092

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-15: Auto-dismiss toasts after 4 seconds, except action toasts
**should**. Auto-close toasts after 4000ms by default, except a toast that carries an action button (Undo, Retry): it stays until the person acts on it or dismisses it (Sonner: duration: Infinity on that toast() call).
- Values: duration: 4000ms; action-toast: no auto-close: duration: Infinity on that toast() call, until the person acts or dismisses it [inferred]
- Why: 4000ms is Sonner's default duration: by default the toast disappears after 4 seconds unless you hover over it. A toast with an action is the exception: closing it on a timer puts a time limit on the action, and the accessibility floors outrank every house standard (docs/KNOWLEDGE.md section 2; WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable), so it persists; this agrees with DC-L08-18 and the Q-form-04 option inline-banner [inferred: no source states the exception].
- Sources: S-L19-006, S-L19-021, S-L19-091, S-L19-089

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-16: Pause the toast timer on hover
**should** · web. Pause the auto-dismiss timer while the pointer hovers the toasts.
- Why: The toast disappears after 4 seconds unless you hover over it, so a person reading it keeps it.
- Sources: S-L19-006

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-17: Pause toast timers in a hidden tab
**must** · web. Pause the auto-dismiss timer while the document is hidden (document.hidden and the visibilitychange event).
- Values: api: document.hidden + visibilitychange; hook: useIsDocumentHidden
- Why: A toast fired while the person is on another tab would otherwise time out unseen; an inactive tab should freeze its toasts.
- Sources: S-L19-006, S-L19-023

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-18: Swipe toasts away along their position
**should**. Let people swipe or drag toasts and drawers away, on touch devices and on desktop; for toasts the allowed swipe directions follow the toaster position, and swipeDirections is overridden only when they must differ.
- Values: swipeDirections: based on position (default)
- Why: People are used to swiping notifications away on their devices, and Sonner derives the swipe directions from the position.
- Sources: S-L19-006, S-L19-021, S-L19-022, S-L19-005

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-19: Pick the toast call by need
**should** · react. Pick the toast() call by what the message needs: toast('Title') with { description } for plain messages, toast.success/error/info/warning for status, toast.promise for work tied to one promise, toast.loading plus an update by id when you manage the states yourself, { action } / { cancel } for buttons, and toast.custom for headless JSX.
- Values: plain: toast('Title', { description }); status: toast.success / toast.error / toast.info / toast.warning; promise: toast.promise(promise, { loading, success, error }); manual-async: toast.loading('…') then toast.success('…', { id }); action: { action: { label, onClick } }; event.preventDefault() keeps it open; cancel is the secondary button; custom-shell: toast(<jsx />); headless: toast.custom((t) => <jsx />)
- Why: Typed calls carry the matching icon, the promise toast starts loading and switches to success or error on its own, and the action button closes the toast unless onClick calls event.preventDefault().
- Sources: S-L19-022, S-L19-021, S-L19-091, S-L19-091, S-L19-006

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-20: Promise toasts need a settling promise
**must** · react. Pass toast.promise a promise, or a function returning one, that actually resolves or rejects.
- Why: Otherwise the loading toast waits forever and never closes.
- Sources: S-L19-022, S-L19-022

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-21: Update a toast by its id
**should** · react. To change a toast already on screen, keep the id toast() returns and call toast() (or a typed call such as toast.success) again with that id, passing only the props that change, instead of adding a new toast.
- Values: example: const id = toast.loading('Uploading…'); toast.success('Uploaded', { id });
- Why: Calling toast() with the same id updates the existing toast, only the props you pass change, and a typed call switches its type.
- Sources: S-L19-022, S-L19-089, S-L19-021

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-22: Toasts follow the app theme
**must** · react. In an app with a dark theme, set the Toaster theme to 'system' or pass the theme provider's resolved theme (for example <Toaster theme={resolvedTheme} /> from next-themes).
- Values: theme: theme="system" or theme={resolvedTheme}; default: 'light'
- Why: theme defaults to 'light' and does not track the OS, so dark mode is otherwise ignored.
- Sources: S-L19-022, S-L19-021, S-L19-092

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-23: Rich colors and invert from defaults
**should** · react. Start toast styling from Sonner's defaults: add richColors on the Toaster when success and error must read green and red, and use invert only to flip toasts against the theme.
- Values: richColors: false (default); invert: false (default)
- Why: Success and error toasts are gray by default; richColors and invert are the first rung of the styling ladder.
- Sources: S-L19-022, S-L19-022

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-24: Headless toast for the design system
**should** · react. Build the design system's toast headless with toast.custom() and your own JSX, wrapped in your own toast() function. Climb the styling ladder (defaults, inline style, classNames, headless) only as far as a change needs: the middle rungs suit a few small changes, and a design-system toast should not linger there.
- Values: headless: toast.custom((t) => <jsx />); small-change: toastOptions={{ style: { … } }}; avoid: unstyled: true (a halfway house; headless gives more control for the same effort)
- Why: Headless keeps Sonner's positioning, stacking and swipe while giving full control, and it is the recommended approach because people usually either use the defaults or go fully custom; styling parts with classes gets messy quickly and is a good compromise only for a few changes.
- Sources: S-L19-022, S-L19-022, S-L19-090, S-L19-090

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-25: Toast classNames need !important
**must** · css, react. When styling toast parts through toastOptions.classNames (toast, title, description, actionButton, cancelButton, closeButton), mark every class !important (Tailwind: the ! prefix) unless the toast is unstyled, and go headless once more than a few classes need it.
- Values: parts: toast, title, description, actionButton, cancelButton, closeButton; tailwind: !text-red-900
- Why: Sonner's injected styles win the cascade, so classes without !important have no effect.
- Sources: S-L19-022, S-L19-021, S-L19-090

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-26: Set toast defaults on the Toaster
**should** · react. Put app-wide toast options in the Toaster's toastOptions and override them per toast() call only where needed.
- Values: prop: toastOptions
- Why: Options passed to toast() override the same options set on the Toaster.
- Sources: S-L19-021, S-L19-091

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-27: Target toasts when several toasters exist
**must** · react. When more than one Toaster exists, give each an id and pass toasterId in every toast() call.
- Values: example: <Toaster id="canvas" />; toast('…', { toasterId: 'canvas' })
- Why: Without toasterId, every toaster renders the toast.
- Sources: S-L19-022, S-L19-021

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-28: Handle dismiss and auto-close separately
**should** · react. Handle user dismissal in onDismiss and timeouts in onAutoClose, and wire both when code must react to every way a toast closes.
- Values: callbacks: onDismiss, onAutoClose
- Why: onDismiss fires on the close button or a swipe and onAutoClose fires when the toast closes after its duration; there is no single closed callback.
- Sources: S-L19-022, S-L19-089

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-29: Toasts default to bottom-right
**should** · web, react. Place toasts bottom-right by default, choosing only from top-left, top-center, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-center and bottom-right.
- Values: default: bottom-right; positions: top-left, top-center, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-center, bottom-right
- Why: bottom-right is Sonner's documented default and these are its six positions; swipe directions follow the position.
- Sources: S-L19-021, S-L19-092

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-30: Toaster edge offsets: 32px and 16px
**should** · web, react. Offset the toaster 32px from the screen edges on desktop and 16px when the screen is narrower than 600px (offset and mobileOffset).
- Values: offset: 32px; mobileOffset: 16px; mobile-below: 600px
- Why: These are Sonner's documented default offsets, and mobileOffset applies below a 600px screen width.
- Sources: S-L19-092, S-L19-022, S-L19-021

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-33: Copy Sonner styles into shadow DOM
**must** · web. When rendering Sonner inside shadow DOM, copy the <style> elements in document.head whose text includes [data-sonner-toaster] into the shadow root.
- Values: selector: [data-sonner-toaster]
- Why: Sonner inserts its styles into the document head when the bundle loads, so they are not available inside shadow DOM.
- Sources: S-L19-089, S-L19-022

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-34: Import Sonner styles when they are lost
**should** · web. When toasts render unstyled (Astro, view transitions), import Sonner's stylesheet explicitly in a layout: import 'sonner/dist/styles.css'.
- Values: import: import 'sonner/dist/styles.css'
- Why: Sonner's injected stylesheet was lost.
- Sources: S-L19-089, S-L19-022

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-35: Toast API is a plain function
**should** · react. Expose the design-system toast as a plain toast() function callable from anywhere, with one <Toaster /> mounted once: no hooks and no React context.
- Values: api: toast('My toast'); state: observer pattern: <Toaster /> subscribes, toast() notifies
- Why: No hooks, no context, one insert and a function call is one of the two reasons Sonner succeeded; the less friction to adopt, the more people use it (Sonner avoids context with an observer pattern).
- Sources: S-L19-006, S-L19-006, S-L19-023

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-37: Prefer drawers over modals on mobile
**should** · web, ios, android. On mobile, present secondary content in a drawer (bottom sheet) rather than a modal.
- Why: A drawer gives a more native feel on mobile.
- Sources: S-L19-005

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-38: Build drawers on an accessible dialog
**should** · react. Build drawers on an accessible dialog primitive (Vaul builds on Radix Dialog) with composable, styleable parts: Root, Trigger, Portal, Overlay, Content, Handle, Title, Description and Close.
- Values: parts: Drawer.Root, Drawer.Trigger, Drawer.Portal, Drawer.Overlay, Drawer.Content, Drawer.Handle, Drawer.Title, Drawer.Description, Drawer.Close
- Why: The dialog primitive makes the drawer accessible and handles focus management, a Radix-like API feels familiar, and not every drawer has to look the same. Vaul itself is unmaintained per its GitHub README (learn/sources.json, checked 2026-09-24); flag that before adding it as a dependency.
- Sources: S-L19-005, S-L19-005, S-L19-093

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-39: Drawer defaults: modal, bottom, dismissible
**should** · react. Default drawers to modal, opening from the bottom edge, dismissible (outside click, Escape and drag down), draggable from anywhere rather than only the handle, and portalled with an overlay over the inert rest of the view.
- Values: modal: true; direction: bottom; dismissible: true; handleOnly: false; container: document.body
- Why: These are Vaul's Root defaults; dismissible: false blocks all three ways of closing, and the Overlay covers the inert portion of the view. Vaul itself is unmaintained per its GitHub README (learn/sources.json, checked 2026-09-24); flag that before adding it as a dependency.
- Sources: S-L19-093, S-L19-093, S-L19-097

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-40: Drawer curve: cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)
**must**. Animate drawers and sheets that open or close on a timing curve (every web drawer) with the iOS-like drawer curve, defined once as a token: --ease-drawer: cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1) (React Native: EASE_SHEET = Easing.bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)). Sheets and drawers a finger drives on iOS and Android settle with a spring instead (STD-springs-gestures-08).
- Values: --ease-drawer: cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1); react-native: EASE_SHEET = Easing.bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1); native-sheet: spring { duration: 300, dampingRatio: 0.8, velocity }
- Why: The curve, from the Ionic Framework, closely matches iOS's sheet; the right easing and duration make a big difference to how the component feels, and built-in CSS easings are too weak.
- Sources: S-L19-005, S-L19-018, S-L19-023, S-L19-025, S-L19-033, S-L19-024, S-L19-016, S-L19-015, S-L19-017

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-44: Drag a drawer only from its scroll top
**should**. Let a scrollable drawer be dragged only when its content is scrolled to the top, and block dragging for 100ms after scrolling reaches the top.
- Values: check: shouldDrag; drag-lock-after-scroll: 100ms
- Why: Being scrollable and draggable at once is tricky; this mirrors native iOS drawers, and fast scrolling can overshoot the top into a drag with enough velocity to close the drawer by accident.
- Sources: S-L19-005, S-L19-005

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-45: Keep drawer inputs above the keyboard
**should** · web, react. When an input inside a drawer opens the on-screen keyboard, stop the browser's scroll-into-view and use the Visual Viewport API to size the drawer to the visual viewport and sit it directly above the keyboard (Vaul: repositionInputs, on by default).
- Values: listener: window.visualViewport resize; height: `${visualViewportHeight - OFFSET}px`; bottom: `${Math.max(diffFromInitial, 0)}px`, where diffFromInitial = window.innerHeight - visualViewportHeight; vaul: repositionInputs: true (default)
- Why: Otherwise the browser scrolls up and pushes the drawer, potentially hiding important content; sitting above the keyboard keeps the drawer fully scrollable, and the author found this works best despite a slight delay. Vaul itself is unmaintained per its GitHub README (learn/sources.json, checked 2026-09-24); flag that before adding it as a dependency.
- Sources: S-L19-005, S-L19-096, S-L19-093

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-48: Fixed-pixel snap points for inputs
**should**. Use a fixed-pixel snap point (rather than a fraction of the viewport) when something such as an input must stick out by the same amount on every device.
- Values: forms: fraction of the viewport or fixed px
- Why: Fixed values make the content stick out evenly on all devices.
- Sources: S-L19-005

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-59: React Native: native sheet presentations
**must** · react-native. In React Native (Expo Router), present a bottom sheet that is its own screen with presentation: 'formSheet' (with detents for a short interruption such as a picker, filter or share), use presentation: 'modal' for a self-contained task the user can abandon, and build a custom drag-to-dismiss sheet only when it must live inside an existing screen.
- Values: sheet-screen: presentation: 'formSheet'; short-interruption: presentation: 'formSheet' with sheetAllowedDetents; abandonable-task: presentation: 'modal'
- Why: formSheet is a real UISheetPresentationController, free and correct; the navigation table maps each overlay kind to a presentation.
- Sources: S-L19-016, S-L19-015, S-L19-015

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-60: React Native: form sheets on both platforms
**must** · react-native, android, ios. Design React Native form sheets for both platforms: at most three detents, content that is a single screen (use presentation: 'modal' if it needs its own navigation), a drag affordance beyond sheetGrabberVisible, and explicitly sized content for sheetAllowedDetents: 'fitToContents'.
- Values: max-detents: 3; grabber: sheetGrabberVisible is iOS-only; fit: sheetAllowedDetents: 'fitToContents' needs explicit size, not flex: 1; nested-navigation: presentation: 'modal'
- Why: Android caps detents at three and silently truncates longer lists, cannot host native headers or nested stacks in a form sheet, and shows no grabber; a flex: 1 root has no intrinsic height to fit.
- Sources: S-L19-015, S-L19-015, S-L19-015, S-L19-015

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-65: Safari theme bar must match the overlay
**should** · web. Sync Safari's theme-color with a drawer overlay only if it stays in step with the overlay: precompute the opaque color the overlay makes over the background, interpolate to it along the drawer's own curve when the drawer opens, pick the color from a linear interpolation by drag progress while dragging, and leave the sync out if it falls out of step.
- Values: meta: meta[name="theme-color"]; curve: bezier-easing with the drawer curve
- Why: Linear interpolation will not match a drawer on a custom bezier curve, and the author has not shipped the theme-bar sync in Vaul because it does not match the overlay transition when frames drop.
- Sources: S-L19-005, S-L19-005

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-72: Feedback on press, commit on release
**must**. Show press feedback the instant the pointer or finger goes down (:active, or pointerdown / onPressIn when JavaScript is needed) and commit the action on release; never show feedback only on click.
- Values: css: :active; js: pointerdown; react-native: onPressIn (feedback), onPressOut (commit)
- Why: Waiting for click or touch-up to show anything feels dead and reads as lag even at 0ms, because the finger has already left.
- Sources: S-L19-020, S-L19-016, S-L19-028

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-77: Hold to confirm: slow press, fast release
**must** · web, css. When a destructive action that a plain click fires too easily uses hold-to-confirm, make the press slow and the release fast: an overlay clipped to inset(0 100% 0 0) fills to inset(0 0 0 0) over 2s linear while pressed and snaps back over 200ms ease-out on release, with scale(0.97) on the button.
- Values: rest: clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0); pressed: clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0); transition: clip-path 2s linear; release: transition: clip-path 200ms var(--ease-out); button: transform: scale(0.97)
- Why: Be slow where the person is deciding and snappy where the system responds (symmetric timing on a hold is a review finding); linear is right because the fill is a progress indicator.
- Sources: S-L19-017, S-L19-023, S-L19-018, S-L19-032

### STD-components-toasts-drawers-78: Dismiss toasts from code by id
**should** · react. Remove a toast from code with toast.dismiss(id), using the id that toast() returns (or t.id inside toast.custom), and call toast.dismiss() with no id only when every visible toast should go.
- Values: one: const id = toast('Event has been created'); toast.dismiss(id);; all: toast.dismiss(); headless: toast.custom((t) => <jsx />): t gives the id to dismiss
- Why: toast.dismiss(id) is the documented way to remove a toast programmatically; called without an id it dismisses all toasts at once.
- Sources: S-L19-089, S-L19-022, S-L19-021
